wintercity_e13_entry.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_entry.text: On Day 899, Yue paid eight copper for the inn week through Day 905 before going to the public sample appointment. The thirty-two-copper journey reserve and Day 912 clinic fee stayed separate. Her completed money could cover this present bed; the proposed seasonal wage had not yet been earned. The sky was pale above the heat court, with smoke leaning away from the north roofs. She carried only the light sample sheet and current task restriction.

wintercity_e13_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_001.text: Qiao Ning placed the public notice on the seated stand and asked Yue to read it as if a caller had missed the first sentence. The sample lasted twenty minutes under a disclosed assessment agreement, with no customer queue or productive paid shift concealed inside it. Yue would receive no wage for this application sample, and the desk would not make applicants fill a whole morning for free. She accepted that bounded condition before beginning.

wintercity_e13_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_002.text: The notice described a gate route changed for maintenance. Yue read the current date first, then the route and its actual hours. Ning asked which entrance a caller should use after the early closing. Yue gave the named alternative instead of promising the closed one would wait. She did not use the station score as a reason to certify the answer. The public sheet and present desk authority supplied the information this ordinary task required.

wintercity_e13_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_003.text: A word had been smudged in the sample. Yue asked for the actual clean copy rather than guess it from the rest of the sentence. Ning provided one and marked the request as appropriate. Speed was part of keeping a queue moving; it did not outrank correct location and hours. Yue took the planned brief posture pause. The sample tested whether the actual role fit her current restriction, not whether discomfort could be overcome by wanting the job more intensely.

wintercity_e13_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_004.text: At the end, Ning offered the authorized seasonal seat under its written terms. Yue accepted three three-hour mornings each week for nine weeks, two copper per completed hour. The first sessions would be Days 900, 902, and 904; the first eighteen-copper settlement would occur on Day 906 after those nine hours were completed. The grant's total maximum remained one hundred sixty-two across the full term. Neither signature made the future amount payable now.

wintercity_e13_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_005.text: The paid keeper would handle all registers, writing, and carrying. Breaks were part of the accepted roster, with the arm kept within its current ordinary limit. The role concerned already public service information, not apparatus certification or confidential testimony. If her condition worsened, Yue would report it and stop the actual unsafe task. An uncovered missed hour would not be earned. Ning gave her the agreed copy so sympathy could not later be mistaken for a different employment promise.

wintercity_e13_006.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_006.text: The other eligible reader asked about the decision outside. Yue said she had accepted the morning seat. Ning gave the other reader the actual afternoon proposal's status: its separate funding was still under review. No imaginary replacement wage was offered to make disappointment disappear. The reader thanked them for a clear answer and left to ask at another desk. Yue watched her go without treating the woman's continued search as a private debt she could solve with unearned money.

wintercity_e13_007.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_007.text: Mrs Fen asked whether the new job would change the inn's breakfast time. Yue could order the same early bowl on her three appointed mornings and pay its listed ordinary price. The other days would retain their own choices. Fen put the request on the actual kitchen list rather than grant a permanent free breakfast to a public reader. Yue liked having a small practical part of the next morning settled before it arrived.

wintercity_e13_008.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_008.text: On Day 900, the keeper set the current sheets on the stand before the public queue opened. A date strip showed which copies had replaced older notices. Yue read the waiting hours to the first callers, then asked one who seemed uncertain to name the route he intended to take. He had confused the north gate with the west passage. Repeating both locations helped him choose the actual open route without collecting his name for an unrelated future dispute.

wintercity_e13_009.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_009.text: The morning's three hours included the agreed pauses. The keeper handled written requests while Yue rested her posture; another reader was not secretly required to cover the pauses unpaid. Callers could see the roster and the next reading time. One complained about waiting. Ning offered the printed sheet or the scheduled spoken interval. A public service could be useful and finite without promising immediate attention to everyone who happened to arrive.

wintercity_e13_010.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_010.text: A woman with a private heating invoice wanted Yue to say the charge was unlawful. Yue could point to the dispute clerk and read the listed application requirements, but would not pronounce on a bill she had not been hired or qualified to adjudicate. The woman took the address and kept her invoice. Yue returned to the current notice. Declining an unauthorized judgment preserved the caller's actual chance to bring the case to someone who could hear it.

wintercity_e13_011.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_011.text: After the first session, the keeper entered three actual completed hours and Yue confirmed the date. No eighteen-copper payment was issued yet; the week's remaining six hours still had to occur. The task had not increased her arm pain. She took the light route home and ate a one-copper simple meal. The morning had given her useful ordinary work without any new powered clearance. Her rested voice was not a substitute for the forearm's scheduled assessment.

wintercity_e13_012.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_012.text: On Day 901, she had no seasonal reading session. She walked as far as the public bench where snowmelt ran along the drain. A cleaner paid to clear that drain asked bystanders to use the other side while the grate was lifted. Yue complied without trying to help raise it. The cleaner's rope, grip, and ordinary colleague were adequate for the work already planned. Her absence from the lifting did not leave the city waiting for a heroine to act.

wintercity_e13_013.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_013.text: She met Bai Jia carrying a covered tray toward the repaired stall. Jia had booked an ordinary assistant for the busiest hour and had no reason to borrow Yue's injured arm. They shared a brief conversation about the festival's early crowds. Jia wanted to try a sweeter bean filling, but would need enough customers to cover the actual sugar price. Yue offered an opinion about taste and left the purchase decision with the person paying for the stock.

wintercity_e13_014.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_014.text: At the court, the service notice had changed again. North Kestrel Works would end the optional staffed waiting corner at its private yard after Day 907, when the current inspected term expired. Its public entrance route would still have to honour the existing posted passage agreement during its actual hours. Yue read both clauses carefully. The owner had not cancelled every public service because he won a contest. He had chosen not to renew a finite additional private-room arrangement.

wintercity_e13_015.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_015.text: The loss of that corner mattered to people whose work ended before the wider public room opened. A private calendar could be lawful and still create a practical gap. Yue took the notice to Ning during the desk's ordinary question period, asking which existing route would remain rather than demanding an unfunded replacement. Ning showed the public open bench and its fixed hours. There was a real uncovered interval, and no extra keeper already paid to erase it.

wintercity_e13_016.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_016.text: Ning said a request for another staffed interval would need a funded proposal, eligible space, safety inspection, and someone authorized to accept the duties. Yue could help describe the gap as her own public observation. She could not promise that every worker wanted the same solution or spend a cooperative's money without its members. She copied the current published closing dates and left private client names out. The future problem now had a finite shape that an actual hearing could evaluate.

wintercity_e13_017.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_017.text: A man from the factory said winning the comparison should have settled whether Gao Shen could decide the corner's hours. Yue answered that the owner had indeed won the physical contest. The room's inspected term and public passage agreement governed different questions. She did not claim the owner's larger qi reserve was irrelevant to his apparatus qualifications. It simply did not supply a completed renewal document or pay the keeper whose shift would otherwise be missing.

wintercity_e13_018.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_018.text: Another person said Yue's defeat proved she should not speak about any room. Ning asked whether her submitted question required a powered qualification. It did not; the public notice and hours could be read by an ordinary eligible applicant. Yue was glad the clerk could keep that distinction without inventing a heroic victory. She could acknowledge being physically weaker and still ask whether an early worker had somewhere actually open to wait.

wintercity_e13_019.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_019.text: On Day 902, the second seasonal morning began with the changed room notice on the current stand. Yue read the expiry date plainly and explained the remaining public route. She could not announce a hoped-for replacement as if it were already staffed. A caller chose a later journey after hearing the true gap. Another used the open bench within its existing hours. Their different choices were useful evidence of actual need only if they later consented to its appropriate use.

wintercity_e13_020.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_020.text: Yue kept no private record of those callers. The public task did not authorize named interviews, and a desire to improve service did not expand its source permissions. She could note that several people asked the same public question without claiming their individual support. Ning handled the formal applications from people who chose to submit them. Some declined to leave any paper. Their ability to receive information survived that refusal.

wintercity_e13_021.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_021.text: During the scheduled pause, the keeper discovered that an older copied sheet still sat beneath the new notice. It was removed before another caller received it. Yue asked for the replacement date to remain visible on both spoken and printed versions. The desk accepted that ordinary practice within its own authorized work. It was a small preventive correction with a concrete effect: tomorrow's reader would not have to infer which room calendar the loose stack described.

wintercity_e13_022.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_022.text: At the end of the second three-hour session, the week's account showed six hours completed, with three still scheduled for Day 904. Yue did not spend eighteen copper before the remaining work and settlement. She took the receipt copy home and kept it beside the accepted seasonal term. The oral role was independent of factory wages already closed. Losing private access later could matter while this separately funded public task remained a real current source of ordinary income.

wintercity_e13_023.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_023.text: Wen had finished the two repairs that kept her from the contest's full afternoon. She brought a palm-sized sketch made by an apprentice, showing the umbrella's repaired seam, not a portrait of Yue's defeat. She laughed at how carefully the drawing enlarged one crooked stitch. Wen said the buyer cared about that seam in the rain. Her ordinary finished work had its own stakes. She did not ask Yue to become a judge of the apprentice's whole future from one sheet.

wintercity_e13_024.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_024.text: She spent a short interval with her in the common room. The conversation drifted toward a possible summer stall and back to the winter orders actually booked. Wen had not paid for a summer site and would not call the idea a guaranteed shop. Yue could enjoy hearing it while asking about the next real repair. They had room for hopeful thought without turning it into cash or an institution that would be available before the actual lease was signed.

wintercity_e13_025.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_025.text: On Day 903, the festival committee opened an ordinary rehearsal to visitors. Yue sat at the edge where she could leave without crossing the puppet frame's working space. Peng's paid helper adjusted the frame while the younger operator checked each string. The child who had written the stove verse wanted the last rhyme kept. Peng had done so after the actual discussion. Yue could hear how the shorter version made room for the audience's laughter.

wintercity_e13_026.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_026.text: A sponsor asked whether the puppets could carry North Kestrel Works' name across the final curtain. The committee had sold one listed acknowledgement, not control of every line. Its keeper showed the accepted scope and offered that actual acknowledgement. The sponsor could decline renewal next time. He could not silently rewrite a child's verse because the owner had won a physical comparison elsewhere. Yue watched the small dispute settle under the committee's own documents and people.

wintercity_e13_027.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_027.text: Peng asked Yue if she would read one ordinary narration line while the helper adjusted the strings. It was an unpaid rehearsal favour lasting less than a minute, not a permanent performing post. Yue agreed within her current voice and posture limits, holding no heavy script. The line was about a household finding enough kindling for a cold evening. The child laughed at the stove's exaggerated complaint. Yue returned the borrowed page when her small part was finished.

wintercity_e13_028.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_028.text: The younger operator missed a cue and wanted to restart from the beginning. Peng chose to repeat only the short difficult passage, allowing the already paid helper to finish on time. The choice changed what they could practise before the booked room closed. No one was forced to stay another unpaid hour so the performance could feel perfect. Yue recognised the same finite calendar she had been learning at the service desk, expressed now in wood, cloth, and a frustrated child.

wintercity_e13_029.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_029.text: Outside the rehearsal, Rao Jun sold a repaired pane to a customer who had measured the opening incorrectly. Jun could trim this pane within the paid allowance, but a larger one would need new stock and a different price. The customer chose the smaller repair after checking the actual frame. Yue listened while passing and did not decide the purchase for them. Work could go right because a modest mistake was measured before anyone promised an impossible fit.

wintercity_e13_030.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_030.text: Her forearm tightened during the longer walk home. She stopped on the public bench and let the supported position settle. This was not evidence of a hidden attack by Gao Shen or a new channel opening under pressure. It was ordinary soreness after an injury and a longer interval upright. She shortened the remaining route, bought a simple meal, and made a note to tell Zhou An if the pattern persisted. The current restriction still governed her actual day.

wintercity_e13_031.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_031.text: At the inn, a traveller had arrived without checking whether a room remained. Mrs Fen offered the last shared space at its listed price, or directions to another house. The traveller wanted Yue to surrender her paid room for the night because she already knew the city. Yue could sympathize and decline. Fen did not confiscate a current paid booking to make the unexpected arrival easier. The traveller chose the shared space and had an actual bed rather than a promise someone else would be displaced.

wintercity_e13_032.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_032.text: The incident left Yue feeling ungenerous until she looked at the clinic support and tomorrow's appointed work. Her room was part of an ordinary recovery and employment plan she had paid for. She could offer the traveller the public meal times without offering every owned thing in the name of being useful. He accepted the information the next morning and did not ask again. They could become neighbours for one night without either acquiring an unlimited claim on the other.

wintercity_e13_033.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_033.text: During the quiet afternoon of Day 903, Chen Rui's next ordinary letter arrived at the inn through the paid route he had chosen. It answered Yue's earlier acknowledgement, not a contest result she had not yet sent him in that exchange. He wrote about the limits of a useful advocate's memory: a familiar account could still contain a mistaken date. He had checked his own notes before offering another comment on a clause they had actually seen.

wintercity_e13_034.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_034.text: The letter asked whether she had kept the final inventory rather than assuming an owner would remember it. Yue could answer yes under whichever completed employment account she actually held. She could not tell him she possessed private factory sources if her selected role had never granted them. The earlier bounded reading had not created a permanent client file. Chen Rui offered no further unrequested service and made no claim to be travelling toward the city to solve her next difficulty.

wintercity_e13_035.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_035.text: She wrote an ordinary acknowledgement in short intervals and paid the one-copper dispatch fee. It said she had kept the proper closure and was considering public service questions independently. She did not send customer names, private methods, or another person's supposed consent. The letter gave a distant friend a true limited update. If she later wanted formal help, it would need a new actual agreement rather than an expectation that friendship supplied endless professional hours.

wintercity_e13_036.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_036.text: The inn's retired tin worker, Chen Bo, had been listening to the festival practice through the open window. He asked Yue whether the child who wrote the stove verse had ever lived beside a noisy flue. Yue did not know. Bo laughed and said the rhythm sounded like one that rattled at his first workshop. He described the ordinary wedge that finally stopped it. The repaired flue had no spiritual source; someone had simply measured where the loose metal touched.

wintercity_e13_037.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_037.text: Yue asked whether the wedge had been his idea. Bo said his colleague had proposed it, and he had initially dismissed it because the fix seemed too small for the noise. He admitted that with enough humour to keep the memory from becoming a lesson he forced on everyone. Yue liked the answer. She had been tempted to make the contest explain every flaw in her character, when some of what she needed was a clear release and a correctly funded clinic visit.

wintercity_e13_038.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_038.text: Bo showed her a small tin cup whose handle had been repaired three times. He did not ask her to repair it with qi or hold its full hot weight. He turned it on the table and pointed to the oldest join. The cup had belonged to his sister, who still wanted that one rather than a new matching set. Value could come from a chosen history, not only from the strongest or newest object available at a market stall.

wintercity_e13_039.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_039.text: Mrs Fen said the cup should not be used if its edge cracked again. Bo agreed, setting sentiment beside the actual safe-use boundary rather than treating one as a reason to erase the other. His sister could keep it on a shelf if the next repair failed. Yue watched the simple decision take shape. They were not required to destroy every old thing or use it dangerously. Someone who owned the cup could choose a different place for it.

wintercity_e13_040.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_040.text: A young resident wanted to learn the repair, and Bo offered a short ordinary demonstration using cold scrap. The resident would buy his own stock for later practice. Yue watched from the chair without volunteering the injured arm. Bo's time was a favour he chose for that interval, not a school opened by someone's admiration. When the resident asked for another morning, Bo said he would check his own calendar first. The first yes did not make every future request compulsory.

wintercity_e13_041.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_041.text: The demonstration produced one uneven seam. Bo showed why the cold pieces sat differently and let the learner identify the gap before explaining it. Yue recognised a patient kind of comparison. The result could be wrong without the learner being hopeless. It could also remain wrong after being praised for effort. The seam needed an actual change to fit its intended use, just as her direct physical result remained a defeat despite her sincere preparation.

wintercity_e13_042.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_042.text: At the common-room door, Wen met a customer who disliked the repaired umbrella's new darker thread. The cloth now held under the ordinary rain test agreed for the repair, but the customer had expected a lighter colour. Wen brought out the accepted sample and showed which thread had been selected. The customer remembered choosing it indoors and asked about replacing it. That would be additional work with a separate finite price, not an invisible free correction of another purchase.

wintercity_e13_043.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_043.text: Wen offered the quoted replacement interval or the umbrella as repaired. The customer chose to keep it after seeing the thread in daylight. Neither had to be declared entirely wrong for the account to close. Yue spoke only when asked whether the colour looked darker by the window, and said it did. Her opinion did not alter the accepted sample or move the customer's money. The umbrella left with a real owner and an actual finished repair.

wintercity_e13_044.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_044.text: The exchange made her think of the application sample she had completed four days earlier at the desk. Its scope had been announced before she agreed. A bounded unpaid assessment was different from making every applicant perform productive shifts without wages. She had checked that distinction rather than assuming every invitation was either kindness or exploitation. Later proposals would require the same attention. Knowing one owner had a greater physical range did not remove the need to read what each actual offer required.

wintercity_e13_045.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_045.text: Peng sent a messenger to ask whether the common room could host a small rehearsal next week. Mrs Fen checked the paid bookings before answering. There was an available afternoon but not the evening the troupe preferred. The messenger took the real offer back to Peng. Yue did not promise to clear the room herself. If the troupe accepted, its performers would need to fit the available interval or seek another space. The inn remained a place with other residents, whose paid bookings occupied the room before an additional troupe could rehearse.

wintercity_e13_046.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_046.text: While the messenger waited, the child author came to ask whether Yue had liked the shortened rhyme. Yue said she had, naming the moment where the stove's complaint ended. The child wanted her to write that comment for the committee. Yue offered a short sentence in her own limited hand and explained she could not produce a whole review today. The child accepted the smaller statement. Praise remained voluntary and accurate, without turning an injured neighbour into a publicity worker.

wintercity_e13_047.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_047.text: She used a few ordinary words and rested afterward. The sentence identified her own reaction, not the opinion of every visitor at rehearsal. Peng could choose whether it suited the actual programme. Yue did not add a fabricated title to make the comment more prestigious. A public reader's paid role was not a theatre critic's office. The modest note could still matter to the child whose verse had made the room laugh.

wintercity_e13_048.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_048.text: Outside, the snow became rain against the warmer ground. Fen's assistant put the ordinary drip tray beneath a leak and booked the roofer for the next available interval. Yue did not climb to the roof or power the old tiles dry. The repair needed suitable weather and a qualified worker. Until then, the covered corridor remained closed at its wet edge. The inconvenience had an actual cause, an ordinary temporary protection, and a next step that would not happen instantly.

wintercity_e13_049.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_049.text: The traveller in the shared room asked whether his paid bed was beneath that leak. It was not, but the usual shortest route to it had changed. Fen showed the longer indoor passage. He could use it without another charge, since ordinary room access was part of his accepted booking. If the bed itself became unusable, that would require a different remedy. They did not settle the hypothetical problem by inventing a dry room already available somewhere else.

wintercity_e13_050.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_050.text: Yue admired how Fen kept the present problem smaller than every imaginable future failure. She could say the corridor was partly closed, the actual bed remained dry, and the roof appointment had been requested. None of those statements guaranteed tomorrow's weather. They gave residents enough real information to make ordinary decisions tonight. Yue wanted her own service reading to work that way, with uncertainty stated where it existed and the current usable route described plainly.

wintercity_e13_051.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_051.text: She remembered the central bar moving against her and allowed the memory to stay uncomfortable. Rest, orientation, or an observer could improve how a person met a stronger force; none made the force disappear. The room's rain problem had no reason to repeat that lesson exactly. It had its own roof, booked repair, and people inconvenienced by a changed passage. Yue could live among several kinds of difficulty without demanding that each one redeem the same defeat.

wintercity_e13_052.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_052.text: The afternoon conversation ended when Bo's ordinary helper arrived to carry his workshop box. Yue did not know whether the helper was a relative or a paid neighbour, and did not supply a family history from the greeting alone. Bo said he had arranged the carrying because his knees were poor on wet steps. The helper accepted the box and its actual weight. They left by the longer safe passage, keeping the common-room demonstration a completed little interval.

wintercity_e13_053.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_053.text: Yue stayed at the table long enough to finish the small acknowledgement, then put the pen away. Her light ordinary handwriting was allowed within the current restriction; continuous hours would not be. She kept the support in its fitted position and waited for the posture ache to settle. Tomorrow's public shift had its breaks scheduled. She could maintain an ordinary useful plan only by taking those limits seriously on the unrostered day as well.

wintercity_e13_054.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_054.text: Fen brought the bought evening bowl and asked whether Yue wanted it upstairs or in the common room. Yue chose the common room because the company felt easier there. The ordinary meal charge was the same. She watched the rain form narrow paths on the window and asked Bo's young learner whether the cold seam had improved. The learner showed the actual second attempt on the scrap, leaving its still uneven edge visible.

wintercity_e13_055.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_055.text: The evening had no new qualified cultivation test and no appointment with Gao Shen. Yue's reserve remained hers, while the arm needed its real further assessment. She could enjoy a repaired cup, an umbrella dispute settled, and a child's shorter verse without converting any of them into an advancement. The city offered more than a stage on which she must prove strength. It also offered people whose ordinary work required her to listen carefully and leave their choices intact.

wintercity_e13_056.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_056.text: Before returning upstairs, she thanked Fen for the present support fastening and the bought meal. The thanks did not settle a nonexistent perpetual care debt. Fen wanted residents to speak before a small problem became a damaged room or missed appointment. Yue said she would. She could make that practical promise without guaranteeing perfect recovery or an untroubled future. It belonged to the next ordinary days they would actually share at the inn.

wintercity_e13_057.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_057.text: On Day 904, the third seasonal reading session began with a wet trail across the entrance stones. The keeper put an ordinary mat at the public edge and told callers about the slippery patch. Yue did not step away from the reader's stand to catch people overhead. The paid floor attendant handled the practical crossing. Her spiritual reserve remained stored; the task asked for clear words, not an improvised powered rescue whose limits no one had assessed.

wintercity_e13_058.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_058.text: A caller wanted to know whether the soon-closing private corner was the only place permitted to wait. Yue read the actual public bench hours and explained the uncovered interval. The caller chose to bring a warm wrap and use the later opening. Another asked about a room for a disabled relative, and Yue sent that separate accessibility question to the authorized desk. An ordinary alternative could help one person while failing to meet another's needs. The first success did not erase the second request.

wintercity_e13_059.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_059.text: Ning said the accessibility application would need the applicant's actual consent and requirements. Yue could not submit private medical facts on behalf of an unknown relative because a caller had mentioned them casually. She offered the public form and kept the conversation within its proper place. The caller took it away to ask the relative. That slower sequence protected the person's agency and gave the later office a real request instead of a well-intentioned invented one.

wintercity_e13_060.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_060.text: During the scheduled break, a factory foreman came to ask who had authorized the public room-gap notice. Ning pointed to the actual published expiry and public service calendar. The notice did not accuse the factory of withholding a room beyond a contract that had ended. It said what would actually be open. The foreman could challenge a wrong date with evidence. He left after checking the copy, without deciding that Yue's physical defeat made the whole office unauthorized.

wintercity_e13_061.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_061.text: The morning's last caller asked for a private recommendation to North Kestrel Works. Yue had no current authority to issue one. Her completed earlier employment and public role supplied actual references within their scope, not a hiring mandate for someone else. She directed the person to the ordinary application desk. The caller frowned, then asked for its hours. Yue read them from the current sheet. A refused extra favour did not need to become a failed conversation.

wintercity_e13_062.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_062.text: At closure, the keeper entered the third session's three hours. Yue had now completed nine for the week, earning eighteen copper payable at the Day 906 settlement. She checked the written total and received its copy. The money was earned but not yet physically received; current food and room still came from her owned completed funds. The distinction would matter if the pay desk closed unexpectedly. She kept enough ordinary cash for the actual interval before collection.

wintercity_e13_063.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_063.text: The arm had tolerated the scheduled seated work with the agreed pauses. Yue did not take that as a powered clearance. The clinic had asked for a separate controlled assessment on Day 912, and the restriction remained until then. She could finish useful public reading while declining the heavy register offered by a distracted assistant. The assistant took it back and apologized briefly. A small correction at the doorway prevented a needless strain without making her whole role impossible.

wintercity_e13_064.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_064.text: Day 905 began without a reading shift. Yue walked to the source yard's public board, where Hu Yan had posted the apparatus maintenance dates. The counter-movement station would be unavailable during a scheduled seal inspection. She had no new paid booking to lose, but appreciated knowing the actual calendar before asking about a later observer interval. The yard's public information did not include private operating plans. She read what was posted and left the closed workshop alone.

wintercity_e13_065.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_065.text: Hu Yan came outside with the examiner Luo Pei to compare inspection notes. They greeted Yue and asked whether she had the next clinic appointment confirmed. She gave the date and current limitation, without trying to persuade them that oral work proved the arm ready for apparatus. Yan said a future permitted application would still need its own accepted source and tested control. The old half-unit ceiling described a recovered demonstrated condition; injury could keep the safe present range below it.

wintercity_e13_066.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_066.text: Pei asked whether the public score copy had reached her. Yue said yes and that its result remained plain. He did not offer a new contest to remove embarrassment. The station was not a theatre required to make every losing participant feel redeemed. It was an inspected apparatus with declared conditions, finite staffing, and a result that could be accurately recorded. Yue thanked him for the ordinary care that had followed, then asked only about the public observer process.

wintercity_e13_067.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_067.text: The observer desk could register a future request without guaranteeing a seat before its actual inspection and roster. Yue left her own name under that ordinary rule. There was no fee paid now and no source issued. She would need to decide later whether a real offered interval fit her recovery and work calendar. The request gave her a possible next step, rather than inventing equipment already set aside for the day she wanted to feel strong.

wintercity_e13_068.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_068.text: Near the yard, a group of workers discussed the waiting corner's final day. One wanted a collective replacement proposal; another preferred paid passage to the later room; a third wanted no petition under his name. Yue did not count their overheard words as consented testimony. When they noticed her, she said she could provide the actual public request address. The third worker declined a copy and remained free to use the same public information at another time.

wintercity_e13_069.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_069.text: The first worker asked if a petition required agreement with every complaint about Gao Shen. Yue said a request could state its own finite purpose and source permissions. It did not need to borrow her contest as proof of a heating claim. The workers could choose their own representative and wording. She was not already their delegate because she had noticed the same gap. The conversation ended with one taking the address and the others keeping their own different plans.

wintercity_e13_070.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_070.text: At the inn, the traveller from the shared room paid his actual bill and prepared to leave. He thanked Yue for the meal times and said the shared bed had been tolerable. She was glad without treating the good outcome as proof that everyone could always solve lodging that way. Tomorrow's room availability might differ. Mrs Fen counted the returned key and cleaned the space for its next ordinary booking. A finished one-night problem left no magical extra bed behind.

wintercity_e13_071.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_071.text: The festival drum student came through the court carrying the instrument on its fitted strap. She asked Peng whether an audition practice could use the open rehearsal interval. Peng had a different booking and offered the listed later slot, subject to the committee's actual acceptance. The student chose to apply rather than move another group. Yue heard the exchange from the bench. The city's hopeful young people had their own schedules and disappointments; they did not all owe their next opportunity to her intervention.

wintercity_e13_072.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_072.text: She bought the evening meal and noticed she could hold its light spoon more comfortably than last week. The change was welcome, but she would describe it to Zhou An rather than certify a restored powered range herself. Ordinary recovery could be gradual. Yue did not need the arm to remain equally painful to keep the original defeat honest. Nor did improvement allow her to erase the real money, restricted days, and help that recovery had required.

wintercity_e13_073.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_073.text: Before sleep, she checked the first week's nine-hour receipt and the Day 906 pay desk hours. The next week would begin under the same actual role, with its own sessions and earned eighteen only if completed. No private factory employment had revived through public reading. The waiting corner would still expire on Day 907 under its finite inspected term. Yue could face those separate clocks tomorrow with a paid room tonight and the present injury still included in her plans.

wintercity_e13_074.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e13_074.text: Her next rostered reading morning would be Day 907, followed by Days 909 and 911 in the second week. Yue checked those actual dates against the room notice before putting the papers away. The final private corner opening could still be stated correctly on its last day, without pretending the replacement request had already succeeded.
